subject: zoology
question_text: "Cardiac muscle is highly resistant to fatigue". Justify.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.52, VSAQ 87). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. ADDED BEYOND THE BOOK: the lactic-acid explanation of fatigue is standard physiology; this book's answer stops at the three facts.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three reasons
steps.why: All three facts point one way, to a steady supply of oxygen, so they are listed together before the conclusion is drawn.
common_mistakes: Naming only one reason. Three facts are expected: sarcosomes, myoglobin and blood supply.
Writing haemoglobin for myoglobin. Myoglobin is the oxygen store of muscle.
steps.memory_tip: Three oxygen facts: many mitochondria, plenty of myoglobin, and blood always arriving.
steps.margin_note: Three short facts, one line each.
lines: Cardiac muscle cells hold very many sarcosomes
They hold a large amount of myoglobin, which
The heart muscle has a rich blood supply.

steps.label: The justification
steps.why: Fatigue in muscle comes from lactic acid built up during anaerobic respiration, so a muscle that never runs short of oxygen never fatigues.
common_mistakes: Listing the facts and stopping. 'Justify' asks for the conclusion: respiration stays aerobic, so no lactic acid builds up.
steps.memory_tip: Fatigue comes from lactic acid, and enough oxygen means no lactic acid, so no fatigue.
steps.margin_note: Join the facts to the conclusion in one sentence. That is what 'justify' asks for.

lines.text: Aerobic respiration always, so no fatigue

lines: Because of these, cardiac muscle respires
